batch_node.name: git-serious double-tap: tap repository page v0.6.0
batch_node.description: The tap repository's own page: one page node and five USES_PANEL edges onto git-serious's shared panels, each edge pinning repo=unified-systems-com/tap as a fixed input (tap#359). No panel or search of its own (git-serious-double-tap#11 retired the v0.1.0 copies). v0.3.0 (git-serious-double-tap#32, demo-land 2026-09-10): a sixth row, `findings`, after the open pull requests — the zizmor findings on this repository's workflow files, as a standard table over a search THIS bundle owns (the instance hardcodes the composition; the product-level home for this surface is git-serious-tap#73). Every row opens the finding on /zizmor/finding. Page node upsert (layout) plus one search, one panel and two edges; every prior id is stable, only the batch id moved. v0.4.0 (tap#425): the findings panel declares row_url_template, so a ROW click opens the finding on /zizmor/finding — the consumer names its route; core JS names none. Panel node upsert only. v0.5.0: links into the finding page carry workflow_id — the page seats the workflow's anatomy graph and reads it from the URL (zizmor-tap#33); the collector records location.workflow_id from zizmor-tap#34 on. v0.6.0 (tap#432, 2026-09-11): a seventh row after the security findings — Secrets named by workflows, the first PROJECTION-mode table (rows, not nodes): each workflow's secrets.X names, the ones no readable scope defines, and the scopes read; row click opens the annotated file. Needs tap-plugin-github-core PR# 105 on the grid for the tag to exist and tap#432 for the table to render rows.

node.name: tap
node.description: unified-systems-com/tap, the repository that builds TAP, on its own page. The page owns nothing but its slots: every panel is git-serious's — the generic repository page's identity, machinery and open-pull-requests panels and the landing's status wall and not-observed table — mounted by id, with the page's one privilege carried on each USES_PANEL edge as a fixed input (`inputs: {repo: "unified-systems-com/tap"}`, tap#359) that the page lays over the URL when it builds the panel's address. Polish to a panel lands here the moment it lands on git-serious; ?repo= on this page is ignored because the fixed input wins (git-serious-double-tap#11).

entity.name: double-tap — zizmor findings on one repository's workflow files

node.name: double-tap — zizmor findings on one repository's workflow files
node.description: Every zizmor finding whose FLAGS_WORKFLOW edge lands on a workflow of the given repository. Envelope mode (RETURN f) so the table receives typed nodes; no ORDER BY, because Gryphon refuses it on a traversal (req-grid-gryphon-order-by-envelope) — the table sorts client-side. Cumulative, not current: zizmor does not tombstone yet (zizmor-tap#27), so a finding fixed since it was first seen still appears. Owned by the instance for the 2026-09-10 demo; the product-level home is git-serious-tap#73.

repo.description: The repository's full_name (owner/name). On /double-tap/tap it is pinned by the USES_PANEL edge's fixed inputs, never read from the URL.

node.name: Security findings
node.description: What zizmor finds in this repository's workflow files: injection sinks, unpinned actions, over-broad permissions, dangerous triggers. One row per finding; click a row for the finding in full. Two things this table cannot say: it is every finding ever observed here, not the current state (zizmor does not tombstone yet), and a workflow zizmor could not read shows NOTHING here rather than 'clean' — which workflows were read is the coverage panel's job on /zizmor.

columns.title: Audit
columns.header_tooltip: zizmor's own name for the rule that fired. Click through for the finding in full.

columns.title: Severity
columns.header_tooltip: zizmor's severity: High, Medium, Low, Informational, or Unknown.

columns.title: Confidence
columns.header_tooltip: How sure zizmor is. Low confidence is a hint about reading order, not a false positive.

columns.title: Persona
columns.header_tooltip: Regular, Pedantic or Auditor — which one this is decides whether it is worth acting on.

columns.title: Workflow
columns.header_tooltip: The workflow file the finding is about.

columns.title: Job
columns.header_tooltip: The job the finding sits in. Blank means workflow-level, not unknown.

columns.title: Fragment
columns.header_tooltip: The exact expression the finding is about, when zizmor narrowed to one.

columns.title: Known since
columns.header_tooltip: When this finding was FIRST seen; it does not reset on re-observation.

entity.name: double-tap — the secrets each workflow of a repository names, and which it cannot find

node.name: double-tap — the secrets each workflow of a repository names, and which it cannot find
node.description: One row per workflow of the repository whose body github_core read: every `secrets.X` it names, the ones no readable scope defines (`missing`), and the scopes that were actually read — so an empty `missing` beside a short `scopes_read` is not the same claim as one beside all three (three states, never two). PROJECTION mode (rows, not nodes): the table renders the aliases as columns (tap#432). A workflow with no collected body has no tag and no row — the coverage panel on /zizmor names those. `missing` means named here and defined nowhere the credential could see; on this estate every such name is deliberate (TAP_CORE_RO_PAT went vestigial when the org went public), so the table says 'cannot find', never 'broken'.

query: RETURN w.data.path AS workflow, w.data.tags.secret_refs.referenced AS named, w.data.tags.secret_refs.unresolved AS missing, w.data.tags.secret_refs.scopes_read AS scopes_read, w.data.workflow_id AS workflow_id

repo.description: The repository's full_name; pinned by the slot on /double-tap/tap.

node.name: Secrets named by workflows
node.description: What each workflow file names with `secrets.X`, which of those names no readable scope defines, and which scopes were read. A name in `missing` gets an empty string at runtime and the job runs green — the silent failure this table exists to show. Row click opens the workflow's annotated file.

columns.title: Workflow
columns.header_tooltip: The workflow file. Click the row for the file with every zizmor finding called out.

columns.title: Names
columns.header_tooltip: Every secrets.X the file names inside an expression. GITHUB_TOKEN is the built-in and is not counted.

columns.title: Cannot find
columns.header_tooltip: Names no readable scope defines — org, this repository, its environments. At runtime GitHub hands the step an empty string and the job runs anyway. On this estate these are deliberate: TAP_CORE_RO_PAT went vestigial when the org went public.

columns.title: Scopes read
columns.header_tooltip: Which scopes the collector actually listed. 'Cannot find' is only ever a claim about these.
